plotSections.title: The Door's Reality Tear
bullets: Gerk and Sylan determine that the door is holding open a dangerous distortion and that closing it may cause significant effects.
The door's effects appear connected to movement: opening it while the ship was moving caused reality to stretch along the ship's path, with the ship briefly seeming to exist in two places at once.

The distortion is not limited to the door itself. Individuals can pass through the distorted area, and the ship can physically overlap the doorway without being impeded, suggesting that reality has been stretched between the ship's former and current positions.
Gerk believes he should remain aboard and close the door because he opened it and might die if closing it causes a catastrophic reaction.

plotSections.title: Evacuation and Preparation
bullets: Mahali brings Gerk and Sylan leftover breakfast rolls with preserves and freshly churned butter before they attempt to close the door.

Because the effects of the door are not fully understood, Sylan recommends evacuating the stronghold. Mahali and the residents leave the area, while guards including Koji, Ponchi, and Bo relocate to the tavern.
The party establishes that they have some time before closing the door and prepares ropes and other precautions in case the closure causes them to fall or otherwise be displaced.
Gerk and Sylan proceed with closing the door while Dana, Ciri, and Ord remain involved in preparing for the result.

plotSections.title: Closing the Door
bullets: Gerk steps through the door and again feels a temporal or dimensional shift, described as passing through a semi-thick barrier.
When Gerk shuts the door, reality around the ship stretches and buckles. A quiet physical sound accompanies the closure, followed by a blinding light originating around the former edges of the door.
The light follows the stretched path through the center of the ship, tracing the route between where the ship started and where it ended.
Gerk rolls a 5 on a d10 as part of resolving the door's effects. The DM indicates that this is a middling result and references another chart for the outcome.
The final consequences of the door closure are not yet resolved by the end of this chunk; the DM pauses to allow the players to take any final actions before determining what happened.

Closing the door causes reality around the ship to stretch and buckle, followed by a blinding light tracing the distorted path through the ship.
Gerk rolls a 5 on a d10 to determine the result of the door event; the DM indicates another chart will determine the specific outcome.
The chunk ends while the DM is preparing to resolve the consequences of the door closure.

newTerms.name: Reality Tear / Reality Stretch
notes: A phenomenon produced by the door in which reality appears to stretch between locations, potentially causing objects or locations to overlap or exist in multiple positions.

newTerms.name: Door Closure Chart
notes: A game mechanic used by the DM to determine the consequences of closing the door, involving at least a d10 roll and another chart.

newTerms.name: Doorkeepers
notes: Sylan explicitly identifies the party as the doorkeepers, reinforcing their role and responsibility regarding the mysterious doors.
